newsitem.title: UK: Costain selling last U.S. mining units.
newsitem.headline: Costain selling last U.S. mining units.

text.p: Engineering and construction firm Costain Group, struggling to reduce higher than expected losses, said Tuesday it was selling its U.S. coal units, completing its exit from mining in the United States.
The company said it was selling 52 million pounds ($86 million) worth of assets and restructuring its board as it struggles to refocus amid greater than expected losses.

The group said it was selling its U.S. coal units to Rencoal Inc. for 28.6 million pounds ($47.3 million) and its one-third stake in the Spitalfields development site in London to Malaysia's Metacorp for 23.4 million pounds ($38.7 million).
"Since the announcement of its interim results, the group has become aware of losses significantly greater than forecast," the company said in a statement.

Costain, which clinched a last-ditch survival refinancing in July before plunging deeper into the red, said the sale of its money-losing U.S. coal arm represented the final stage of its exit from U.S. mining.

The company, whose shares have been suspended from trading since Nov. 7, also said that following the financial restructuring and asset sales, current joint Deputy Chairman Azman Firdaus bin Shafii would replace Sir Christopher Benson as chairman.
